C-PREFS-WRITE-TRUTH.Name: Preference write truth: a failed disk write rolls back backend memory and the renderer UI instead of silently surviving the next write or a restart
C-PREFS-WRITE-TRUTH.Summary: Writing a preference is «memory first, disk later, no rollback» on both layers. Backend: PrefsState::set inserts the value into the store map and then saves (src-tauri/src/m005_prefs.rs:320-324) — when save() fails, the rejected value stays in memory and rides the NEXT successful write to disk, so a disk failure is invisible and a value the user believed rejected is silently persisted later; PrefsState::set_many (:332-338) has the same shape for the whole session-profile batch. Renderer: SET_SINGLE_PREFERENCE assigns this[type] BEFORE the write (src/renderer/src/store/preferences.js:808) and swallows a rejection (:815-820, console.error only) — the Settings form, the quick-settings panel and every watcher show and act on a value that was never persisted, and combined with the backend defect the same rejected value lives in renderer state, backend memory and (eventually) disk while every layer pretends it failed. This change makes a failed write impossible to survive: the backend captures the previous values, mutates under the store mutex, and rolls the pre-call values back when the save fails — for set AND set_many, the batch rollback all-or-nothing under the same mutex acquisition so C-SESSION-WRITE-ATOMICITY's one-transaction batch semantics (one lock, one save, one broadcast) stay intact and the C-SESSION-DURABILITY get_many reader can never observe a rejected intermediate state; a loud BLOCK_PREFS_WRITE_ROLLED_BACK marker records the rollback; a test-only set_with_rename seam (the mirror of the existing set_many_with_rename) pins the scout contract — after a failed set(key1) a successful set(key2) does NOT carry key1 to disk, and a re-read store has no key1. The renderer keeps the instant optimistic apply for the happy path but, on a rejected write, restores the previous value, reverts the language side effect, drops the boot-dirty mark and surfaces one localized error notice (raw error console-only); restart permanence is pinned at both layers (a fresh PrefsState::from_path re-read and a fresh hydration carry only accepted values).

Problem.Description: (1) Backend: a failed write survives in memory and is fixed up by the next successful write. PrefsStore::set mutates the map in place (src-tauri/src/m005_prefs.rs:229-231) and PrefsState::set calls guard.set(key, value) then guard.save() (:320-324) — on a save Err the insert is never undone, so the rejected value stays in the live store; the next successful mt_prefs_set/mt_prefs_set_many serializes the WHOLE map and promotes it, silently persisting the earlier rejected value. The test suite pins only the opposite, disk-side angle — set_many_failure_keeps_previous_generation_and_never_promotes_tmp (:766) proves the FILE keeps the previous generation on a failed rename — while the memory side is pinned nowhere (audit SR2:hygiene F-001, scout key PREFS-FAILED-WRITE-LIVES). The injected-rename seam that makes such a pin cheap already exists from C-SESSION-WRITE-ATOMICITY: save_with_rename (:195-216, production save() delegates the real fs::rename to it, :221-223) and the test-only set_many_with_rename (:360-371) — but the seam covers the batch only; there is no single-key set_with_rename, and no pin asserts what a failed SINGLE write leaves behind in memory. The defect class: a transient disk failure (ENOSPC, a vanished profile dir, an injected fault) silently mutates what the NEXT ordinary write persists — user-visible settings truth depends on which write happens to succeed later. (2) Renderer: the UI shows the value before the store accepts it and hides the rejection. SET_SINGLE_PREFERENCE applies defaultEncoding's capability guard first (:796-800, the one honest failure path in the action — a localized error notice and no state change), then assigns this[type] = value (:808), adds the key to bootDirtyKeys (:809), applies the language side effect (:811-813), and only then awaits invoke('mt_prefs_set') inside a try/catch whose catch is console.error alone (:815-820) — no rollback of this[type], no revert of setLanguage, no notice (audit GA:fe-comms F-023, scout key PREFS-UI-EARLY-VALUE). After a rejected write the Settings form, the quick-settings panel and every watcher-driven side effect carry the unpersisted value; the backend (pre-fix) carries the same value in memory, so the lie is mutually consistent until a later write flushes it to disk or a restart (post-fix backend) re-hydrates the truth back out from under the UI. C-PREFS-TRUTH made the READ side honest (schema-driven hydration repair) and its own test contract scopes write semantics out — the write side of the same surface is this bundle's scope.

C-PREFS-WRITE-TRUTH.Relationship: Zone lineage, all read as predecessors: C-PREFS-TRUTH (applied 2026-11-21) owns this zone's READ truth — schema-driven hydration validation with one-shot in-memory repair at the single load point (SET_USER_PREFERENCE) — and its test contract explicitly scopes write semantics out («Write semantics (SET_SINGLE_PREFERENCE) and the Rust store … are out of scope», tests/renderer/store/preferences-load-repair.test.js:17-18); this change is the write-truth half of the same «settings tell the truth» surface, not a duplication: no F-007 repair pin is reworked, the repair-on-load suite keeps passing byte-identically, and a repaired-then-saved value flows through the same write path this change makes honest. C-SESSION-WRITE-ATOMICITY (applied 2026-11-21) built the m005 write machinery this change works inside: the single-transaction set_many (one mutex acquisition, every insert under that lock, exactly one atomic temp+sync_all+rename save, one mt::user-preference broadcast per batch) and the injected-rename test seam (save_with_rename / set_many_with_rename) — its DISK-side contract is binding and untouched (the on-disk profile is already all-or-nothing per generation, pinned at m005_prefs.rs:681 and :766); this change closes the MEMORY half the predecessor left open (the inserts stayed in the map when the save failed) while keeping the one-transaction batch semantics exactly — the rollback is atomic over the whole batch under the same lock, one save, one broadcast, no new command. C-SESSION-DURABILITY (#325, delivered on this base) added the read batch PrefsState::get_many / mt_prefs_get_many (:347-355, :499-509) with the read/write asymmetry law («a read never fans out», strictly read-only, pinned by get_many_returns_requested_keys_without_persisting :815) — the get_many reader is untouched by this change and can never observe a rejected intermediate state because the rollback completes under the same mutex acquisition the write holds; its honesty voice (a failure class never masquerades as a different user-facing fact; the recentlyClosed cannot-tell precedent, recentlyClosed.js:127-143) is the discipline R-2 follows for the renderer notice. Goals.R-1: MEMORY-ROLLBACK (scout key 7, SR2:hygiene F-001, high): a failed preference write can no longer survive in backend memory. PrefsState::set (m005_prefs.rs:320-324) and PrefsState::set_many (:332-338) become transactional on the memory side: the pre-call values are captured, the inserts run, the atomic save runs exactly as today, and on a save Err the pre-call values are restored under the SAME mutex acquisition before the error propagates — a rejected write leaves the store map exactly as it found it, no concurrent reader (get, get_many, all) can observe the rejected intermediate state, and the error still reaches the mt_prefs_set/mt_prefs_set_many commands unchanged (which already return Err before any broadcast, :448 and :477 — a failed write never broadcasts). The save machinery itself (PrefsStore::save / save_with_rename, the temp+sync_all+rename discipline, BLOCK_PERSISTED) is untouched; a rollback logs a loud BLOCK_PREFS_WRITE_ROLLED_BACK marker naming the key (or the batch size for set_many) and the error class. The test seam is the deliberate mirror of set_many_with_rename (:360-371): a #[cfg(test)] set_with_rename(key, value, rename) so pins can fail the final promote of a SINGLE-key write without touching the production path. The failing-first pin failed_set_does_not_survive_the_next_successful_set proves the exact scout contract — a set(key1) whose injected rename fails returns Err AND leaves state.get(key1) == None; the subsequent successful set(key2) persists only the accepted value; a fresh PrefsState::from_path re-read of the store carries key2 and NO key1 («после неудачной set(key1) успешная set(key2) НЕ выносит key1; перечитанный store без key1») — red on the pre-change tree, where the failed insert stays in the map and rides the next save. The batch twin set_many_failure_rolls_every_batch_key_back_out_of_memory proves the same all-or-nothing discipline for the session profile: after a failed set_many, no entry of the batch is in memory and a fresh re-read carries none of them; the disk-side pins set_many_writes_session_profile_in_one_transaction (:681) and set_many_failure_keeps_previous_generation_and_never_promotes_tmp (:766) keep their meaning unchanged.
Goals.R-2: UI-WRITE-CONFIRMATION (scout key 8, GA:fe-comms F-023, high): the renderer stops showing a value the store did not accept, keeping the instant optimistic UX on the happy path. The chosen model, binding: optimistic apply + rollback on rejection + one localized error notice. SET_SINGLE_PREFERENCE (preferences.js:795-821) keeps today's synchronous assignment (:808) and side effects, but on a rejected mt_prefs_set it restores this[type] to the value captured before the write, reverts the language side effect for type === 'language' (setLanguage back to the previous language, :811-813), removes the key from bootDirtyKeys (:809 — the change never became truth), logs a loud console marker naming the key and the error, and surfaces exactly one localized error notice from the new preferences.* keys (severity error, source 'settings' — the in-action defaultEncoding-guard precedent :796-800); the raw error string stays console-only (the C-RENDER-REVIEW-FIXES voice). No retry, no optimistic-value limbo: after the rejection the Settings form, the quick-settings panel and every watcher hold the previous, actually-persisted value, consistent with what a fresh hydration from disk shows and with every other window (which were never told about the rejected value — a failed write broadcasts nothing). The happy path stays byte-identical to today (synchronous apply, exactly one invoke, the BLOCK_INVOKE_OK marker), which keeps every existing consumer pin green unchanged (the quick-settings spies tests/renderer/components/quick-settings.test.js:422 and the Settings-tab suites spying SET_SINGLE_PREFERENCE). Failing-first pins land in a new tests/renderer/store/preferences-write-truth.test.js built on the preferences-load-repair.test.js mock seams (the mocked invoke and notification — :51-53, :64; that suite's contract explicitly scopes write semantics out, :17-18, so this suite is its write-side twin): set_single_preference_rolls_back_the_store_value_when_the_write_is_rejected (red first — today the assigned value survives the rejection), set_single_preference_surfaces_a_localized_write_failure_notice (red first — today the rejection is console.error only, :819), set_single_preference_rolls_back_the_language_side_effect, and the happy-path pins (synchronous apply, exactly one mt_prefs_set, no notice).
Goals.R-3: RESTART-TRUTH (the Wave-4 permanence leg — a failed write survives neither the next write NOR the restart): the rejected value is gone after a restart, proven at both layers. Backend: the R-1 pin's fresh PrefsState::from_path re-read IS the restart leg — the on-disk generation never contained the rejected value, and the rolled-back memory cannot reintroduce it. Renderer: preferences-write-truth.test.js pins a_fresh_hydration_after_a_rejected_write_carries_only_the_persisted_value — after the rejected write and rollback, a fresh store hydration through the real ASK_FOR_USER_PREFERENCE over the persisted profile fixture (the preferences-load-repair.test.js harness) yields the previous value and never the rejected one. Recorded honestly as a meaningful-proof pin rather than a red-first defect detector: the fixture file never contained the rejected value even pre-fix, so the red-first legs of this bundle are R-1's backend pins and R-2's rollback/notice pins — the same honesty convention the predecessor bundle used for its shim-level close-commit pins.
Goals.R-4: Governance: the touched governed files get VERSION bumps and CHANGE_SUMMARY entries per the modification checklist (m005_prefs.rs, preferences.js); the two new locale keys land in all ten locale files gated by tests/renderer/i18n/locale-keys.test.js (the C-SESSION-DURABILITY recently-closed pin precedent, locale-keys.test.js v1.5.0 CHANGE_SUMMARY :32-37; ten locales per the C-10/C-12/C-32/C-56 ten-locale canon); the graph and verification deltas (.grace/graph/runtime.xml, .grace/verification/runtime.xml) land in the same bundle as the code, strictly on the M-005/M-011 and V-M-005/V-M-011 entries, with scenarios naming the new tests; no version change, release, tag or publication is authorized by this specification.

Fix direction is binding, backend: rollback of the captured pre-call values under the same store mutex on save Err — NOT a clone-and-swap of the whole store map (no PrefsStore signature change), NOT a post-failure compensation write (a failing disk must never be written again by the failure path), no change to the atomic save machinery, no new command and no main.rs registration; the C-SESSION-WRITE-ATOMICITY one-transaction batch semantics are preserved exactly (one mutex acquisition, one save, one broadcast per batch) with the rollback atomic over the whole batch.

Fix direction is binding, renderer: optimistic-apply-then-rollback with a localized failure notice — NOT apply-after-confirmation (that would delay every watcher-driven side effect behind an IPC round-trip, change the synchronous contract every consumer pin relies on, and buy no extra honesty over rollback). The rollback itself must not trigger a further persistence attempt (no write loop); side-effect watchers re-running with the restored previous value are expected and idempotent. The notice never claims the value was saved and carries no raw error text (console-only); the notice does not fire on the pre-existing defaultEncoding capability guard, which keeps its own copy (:796-800).

Honesty bar: a failed write is never silent and never survives — Err to the caller plus BLOCK_PREFS_WRITE_ROLLED_BACK (backend), loud marker plus one localized notice (renderer), the rejected value absent from backend memory, renderer state, disk and every restart; markers name preference keys, never file paths, and raw error text stays console-only.

Predecessor contracts stay green and unweakened: the C-SESSION-WRITE-ATOMICITY pins (m005_prefs.rs:681 one-transaction batch, :766 failed rename keeps the previous on-disk generation) and the one-broadcast-per-batch semantics; the C-SESSION-DURABILITY read-only get_many pin (:815) and the read/write asymmetry law; the C-PREFS-TRUTH load-repair and preference-defaults pins; the quarantine pin (:882) and save_is_atomic (:926); npm test, cargo test and the e2e suite stay clean against the recorded pre-existing baseline.

The optimistic-apply-then-rollback model was chosen over apply-after-confirmation (the two options the assignment offered) because the happy path stays byte-identical for every consumer of the synchronous apply contract (the quick-settings/split-view/tabs pin shapes), no watcher-driven side effect is delayed behind an IPC round-trip, and the honesty gain is identical — the rejected value ends up nowhere; the choice is recorded as binding in Constraints.

The rollback-under-the-same-mutex variant was chosen over clone-and-swap (the two options the assignment offered) because it leaves PrefsStore::save/save_with_rename untouched, holds the lock across mutate→save→rollback so no reader (get/get_many/all) can observe the rejected intermediate state, and keeps the batch all-or-nothing by construction; the choice is recorded as binding in Constraints.
